video_title: Has the Bitcoin Price Bottomed? Yes, According to Multiple Metrics
gist: Galaxy head of firmwide research Alex Thorn argues Bitcoin bottomed in late June (~58K) on four pillars: technicals (5-6 weekly closes above the ~75K 50-week MA), positioning (fast-money macro/multistrat funds exited while wealth managers and sovereign funds added), fading old-coin supply, and a stronger debasement case. He calls the bullish view contrarian, names a sustained break below the 50-week MA as the invalidation tripwire, and keeps his 250K-by-end-2027 call.

insights.claim: Historically the 200-week moving average has set the floor of Bitcoin bear markets and the 50-week moving average their ceiling; the only major deviation was post-FTX, when BTC traded meaningfully below the 200-week for several weeks.
insights.speaker: Alex Thorn
insights.so_what: Gives a simple regime map: 200W = bear floor, 50W = bear ceiling / bull floor.
insights.quote: the 200 week has set the floor and the 50we has been the ceiling of bare markets

insights.claim: In every prior Bitcoin bear market (3-4 cycles), multiple weekly closes above the 50-week moving average meant no lower bottom followed; BTC has now had five or six weeks of trading above the 50-week, which sits around $75K.
insights.speaker: Alex Thorn
insights.so_what: If history holds, the late-June ~58K low was the cycle bottom.
insights.quote: multiple weekly closes above the 50 100% of the time basically meant that there was no further lower bottom to come in the bare market

insights.claim: Thorn rejects the small-sample critique of his 50-week MA study, arguing it uses the entire 17-year price history of Bitcoin and that average bear-market length and the four-year cycle also line up with the bottom being in.
insights.speaker: Alex Thorn
insights.so_what: Signal is cycle-consistent but statistically thin; size accordingly.

insights.claim: A sustained drop below the roughly $75K 50-week moving average that is not recovered within a month would invalidate Thorn's bear-market-is-over thesis; each additional weekly close above it strengthens the case.
insights.speaker: Alex Thorn
insights.so_what: Clear risk-management tripwire for longs entered around 80K.
insights.quote: I think the clearest trip wire now is to just watch continued closes over the 50we moving average.

insights.claim: If the late-June low holds, this is the shallowest Bitcoin bear market on record, following the shallowest peak on record (the October 2025 all-time high), indicating cycle magnitudes are compressing as the asset matures.
insights.speaker: Alex Thorn
insights.so_what: Expect smaller drawdowns and smaller upside multiples than prior cycles.
insights.quote: the cycle is compressing in terms of magnitude

insights.claim: Bitcoin ETFs have brought longer-term, slower money into Bitcoin, which Thorn says can buoy bear markets and keep them from going as deep, alongside structurally lower volatility.
insights.speaker: Alex Thorn
insights.so_what: ETF holder base dampens drawdowns.

themes.theme: Positioning: fast money out, sticky money in

insights.claim: CFTC/CME data show both asset-manager net longs and leveraged-trader net shorts in Bitcoin futures are substantially reduced, because the basis trade offers no meaningful advantage over Treasuries or money-market funds today.
insights.speaker: Alex Thorn
insights.so_what: Institutional futures positioning is light, so little forced unwind risk.
insights.quote: that basis trade has basically dried up

insights.claim: Q2 13F filings show macro and multistrat hedge funds such as Brevan Howard, Millennium, Capula and D.E. Shaw massively reduced or exited spot Bitcoin ETF positions, while Morgan Stanley wealth management, Mubadala and Abu Dhabi sovereign wealth funds were the biggest adders.
insights.speaker: Alex Thorn
insights.so_what: Ownership has rotated from fast, equity-correlated money to slow allocators.

insights.claim: Thorn attributes Bitcoin's resilience around $80K during the recent AI-trade selloff to the fact that the funds panicking about AI had already exited Bitcoin, leaving it with no inventory for them to sell.
insights.speaker: Alex Thorn
insights.so_what: BTC's correlation to equity/AI risk-off should be lower than in past cycles.
insights.quote: It's cuz none of the people freaking out about AI own Bitcoin.

insights.claim: Q3 13F filings are due by November 16, the largest filers typically file on the last day, so November 17 is the key date to see Q3 Bitcoin ETF ownership changes.
insights.speaker: Alex Thorn
insights.so_what: Calendar catalyst to confirm or refute the rotation thesis.
insights.quote: November 17th mark your calendar is a very big day

insights.claim: Thorn argues buying now offers a better risk-adjusted entry than trying to catch the bottom at $58K, because the bottom likely happened months ago while the crowd has not yet flowed back in.
insights.speaker: Alex Thorn
insights.so_what: Medium-term long setup for those who believe in eventual new highs.
insights.quote: you have a chance to beat the crowd

insights.claim: Thorn believes the August rally from $58K to $80K was driven by longer-term holders rather than equity traders, making them unlikely to sell in short-term equity turmoil.
insights.speaker: Alex Thorn
insights.so_what: Recent buyers are sticky, reducing downside from equity shocks.

insights.claim: Awakening of long-dormant Bitcoin fell to about 34,000 BTC per month in January-September 2026, down from 47,000 per month in 2025 and 67,000 per month in 2024, which were the largest years of old-coin movement on record.
insights.speaker: Alex Thorn
insights.so_what: OG-holder distribution pressure has eased markedly.

insights.claim: The largest-ever movement of 10+ year dormant coins, in July 2025, was Galaxy facilitating the sale of 80,000 BTC for an OG whale.
insights.speaker: Alex Thorn
insights.so_what: Confirms that dormant-coin awakenings often are real sales.

insights.claim: Thorn expects 2026 old-coin awakenings to come in at less than half of 2025's, framing the 2024-25 distribution as Bitcoin's 'IPO moment' (a Jordy Visser idea) that redistributed supply to higher-price buyers and raised the floor.
insights.speaker: Alex Thorn
insights.so_what: Supply handover largely done; less overhead selling going forward.

insights.claim: US national debt rose from about $23 trillion in 2020 to about $40 trillion today, which Thorn says makes the debasement case for Bitcoin stronger than at the October 2025 high or at the 2009 white paper.
insights.speaker: Alex Thorn
insights.so_what: Fiscal trajectory supports fixed-supply assets.

insights.claim: Thorn argues the AI buildout is debasing either way: it is funded by enormous private credit expansion and tax incentives, and if it fails it is so embedded in retirement accounts and governments that it would likely be bailed out with money printing.
insights.speaker: Alex Thorn
insights.so_what: An AI bust could paradoxically be bullish BTC via bailout liquidity.
insights.quote: I just find it hard to believe that we wouldn't just straight up print money to save the AI build out and the data center buildout ultimately.

insights.claim: Thorn argues AI agents make mass surveillance cheap, raising demand for censorship-resistant money; tokenized deposits and stablecoins are freezable by design, while Bitcoin (and potentially Ether and Zcash) offer an exit valve.
insights.speaker: Alex Thorn
insights.so_what: Privacy/bearer-asset demand is a secular tailwind beyond rate cycles.

insights.claim: Thorn expects AI agents to widely use on-chain programmable money, likely mostly stablecoins and agentic DeFi, because frontier models train on GitHub and public blockchain data structures are highly traversable for AI.
insights.speaker: Alex Thorn
insights.so_what: Agentic DeFi is a near-term product category to watch.

themes.theme: Tokenization hype as a contrarian signal

insights.claim: Thorn says that each time sentiment swung to 'blockchain not Bitcoin' (2014-16, 2018-19, now with tokenization/RWA panels dominating Korea Blockchain Week and the Singapore Token conference), it was a great time to buy Bitcoin and Ether.
insights.speaker: Alex Thorn
insights.so_what: Institutional focus on tokenization over native assets signals light BTC positioning.
insights.quote: each time the pendulum swung this far, it was a great time to buy a Bitcoin.

insights.claim: Thorn expects Bitcoin to be buyable in every brokerage account, not just Fidelity, within roughly one to two years as institutional crypto adoption progresses.
insights.speaker: Alex Thorn
insights.so_what: Distribution expansion is a structural demand driver.

insights.claim: Thorn notes Canton is effectively a permissioned blockchain from Digital Asset, the company founded around 2013 that is on its fourth attempt at the enterprise-blockchain idea.
insights.speaker: Alex Thorn
insights.so_what: Skepticism toward permissioned-chain narratives.

insights.claim: Thorn lists key risks to the Bitcoin thesis as a cryptographically relevant quantum computer or AI-driven cryptographic breaks, catastrophic AI-related hacks, and a major equity or economic shock like March 12, 2020, when BTC fell more than 50% in a day.
insights.speaker: Alex Thorn
insights.so_what: Tail risks to monitor beyond technical tripwires.

insights.claim: Thorn says recent AI anxiety eased after strong SK Hynix results, a KOSPI recovery, a well-received Oracle investor day and FOMC, noting AI 'wall of worry' scares recur roughly every six months.
insights.speaker: Alex Thorn
insights.so_what: Near-term macro overhang for risk assets has lessened.

insights.claim: Thorn's report implies a conservative return to the prior all-time high of about $125K, while he maintains his year-old prediction of $250K Bitcoin by end of 2027; at end-2025 options priced equal odds of $50K or $150K by end-2026.
insights.speaker: Alex Thorn
insights.so_what: ~55% upside to prior ATH, ~3x to the 2027 target from ~80K.
insights.quote: maybe 250 by the end of next year
